A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DRAF research. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including equations, tables and figures, and retained material can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original fairness–accuracy experiments on four benchmark datasets, SPARSEADULT experiments, and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds ACSINCOME results, runtime measurements, multiclass and equalized-odds comparisons, and further diagnostic and robustness experiments.

M1.justification: The original DRAF procedure is retained, but v2 adds substantive adaptations: DRAF-EO combines positive- and negative-label DR penalties, while partial DRAF introduces zero-valued membership indicators for unobserved sensitive attributes (B.5–B.6). These change the training procedure and supported inputs.

E1.justification: v2 retains the original datasets and adds ACSINCOME, five-class COMMUNITIES classification, equalized-odds evaluation on ADULT, and ADULT with missing marital-status information. These broaden task and input-condition coverage. CIVILCOMMENTS' nonbinary attributes were already documented in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparisons with Denis et al. (2024) for multiclass classification and FairICP for equalized odds (Tables 5, 7 and 8), extending comparison to two previously untested settings. The original REG, GF, SEQ and unfair-model comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include maximum classwise disparity, label-specific EO metrics, a runtime sweep from 2^4 to 2^14 groups at n=2^16, subgroup-size stratification using 0.3/0.6 quantiles, and 1% missing marital-status entries. The original experiments' splits and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds learned-weight convergence diagnostics (Figure 5), computational scaling measurements (Table 4), gamma sensitivity separated by subgroup size (Figure 14), and missing-sensitive-attribute robustness testing (Figure 16). The original marginal-group exclusions, gamma sweeps and discriminator ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five random seeds and report average performance. v2 adds no explicit change to replication or inferential uncertainty reporting; its new histograms and boxplots diagnose learned weights and subgroup disparities.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results while retaining the original plotted results unchanged. For example, Table 5 reports multiclass accuracy/disparity of 0.380/0.054 for DRAF versus 0.365/0.056 for Denis et al.; Table 4 reports 127% relative runtime at 2^14 groups. Additional results cover ACSINCOME, EO, convergence and robustness.

T1.justification: The main theorems, assumptions, proofs and Appendix A examples are unchanged apart from numbering and presentation. B.5–B.6 add mathematical definitions for label-specific DR penalties and missingness-aware membership indicators, without new theoretical guarantees for these extensions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's four contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: subgroup-subset fairness, the supIPM surrogate and upper bound, computational efficiency, and favorable performance with sparse subgroups.

C2.justification: v2 interprets weights approaching vertices as evidence of near equality between DR and supIPM. It also refines gamma guidance through subgroup-size findings: medium groups need appropriate thresholds, while tiny groups remain unreliable. The broader sparsity warning and original subgroup-versus-marginal example already existed.

D1.justification: v2 supplies additional experimental recipes, including ACSINCOME attributes and gamma, synthetic runtime-data construction, and missing-attribute encoding. Existing hyperparameter grids, 200-epoch model selection and the supplementary-code availability statement are retained. Detailed reproducibility information for the new extensions remains limited.

R1.justification: v2 adds Denis et al. (2024), Ding et al. (2022), and Lai and Guan (2025), and expands positioning relative to reduction-based fairness methods and equalized-odds approaches. The existing related-work framework is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains intact. v2 locally expands related work and explanations, introduces an extensions subsection, reorganizes Appendix B, clarifies cross-reference labels, and changes author ordering and contribution notes. This is a limited narrative revision rather than wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds convergence histograms, ACSINCOME and missingness plots, subgroup-size boxplots, a subgroup hierarchy diagram, and runtime, multiclass and EO tables. Existing figure images are retained and sometimes relocated or renumbered; title, author-block and heading typography also change.

improvement.justification: v2 provides measured support for scalability and useful tests of subgroup-size limitations and missing-data behavior, strengthening validation beyond v1. The gain is limited by incompletely specified extension setups and inconsistencies in new EO tables: Table 7's FairICP values 0.0342 and 0.0150 average to 0.0246, whereas 0.0238 is printed. These issues temper the benefits of broader empirical coverage.
